title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
abstract: arXiv:2610.31726v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people. We propose a framework for training teaming agents against Cognitively Constrained Partners: simulated partners whose diversity emerges from procedural constraints grounded in human physiological literature, specifically reaction delays and perceptual limitations, rather than from reward shaping or historical training checkpoints. translated_title: 用于实时分区控制中零样本协调的认知受限伙伴
translated_abstract: 有效的人机协作需要能够与不可预测的人类伙伴进行协调的智能体。从实时人类反馈或大型行为数据集进行强化学习成本高昂，而纯模拟训练则会过拟合于人工约定，无法实现与真实人类的零样本协调。我们提出了一个框架，用于针对“认知受限伙伴”训练协作智能体：这类模拟伙伴的多样性来源于基于人类生理学文献构建的程序性约束，具体指反应延迟和感知限制，而非来自奖励塑形或历史训练检查点。在一个改进的“月球着陆器”环境中，我们报告了初步证据，表明这些伙伴的行为比无约束的智能体更像真实人类，并且针对它们训练的智能体能够匹敌最强的交叉对弈基线，同时是唯一一个其性能不依赖于训练方式如何（配置）的智能体。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于人类生理学约束（反应延迟与感知限制）生成多样化模拟伙伴的框架，用于训练人机协作智能体，初步证明这些伙伴的行为更接近真实人类，并能实现与真人的零样本协调。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework for training teaming agents against simulated partners whose diversity emerges from physiologically-grounded cognitive constraints (reaction delays and perceptual limitations), with preliminary evidence showing these partners behave more like real people and enable effective zero-shot coordination.
